about: matrix's layers, checked by tests/test_architecture.py on every test run with the shared checker (components/capabilities/_testing/layers.py), which reads a map as slick crafting-aces' layer-check.py does, so the same file runs under that script too. Adopted from the reviewed map (scratch/review-2026-10-22/matrix-layers.json, at 1580c81) and fitted to matrix as it now is: two runtime ports (an agent session and a model call), the session table, the template. matrix keeps its application services (Executor, BoundAgent, the agent and model steps, Loader) in the domain package; there is no application package. 'why' keys are read by neither checker.
scan_why: Every Python file in the package. Tests are out of scan: a test reaches adapters by design.

why.stdlib: computation (a template's placeholders read with string.Formatter, a session's request digested with hashlib and json), plus the asyncio scheduling, clock, run ids and log records the executor needs to run components
why.pydantic: the one third-party library the core admits: every document and config is a pydantic model, so the core runs with pydantic alone
why.matrix.domain.* by name: listed module by module rather than as the prefix matrix.domain, so the reach into the ports is its own visible allowance, and a new domain module is added here on purpose
why.matrix.domain.ports._out: the application services kept in the domain (Executor, BoundAgent, the steps, Loader, the registry) drive the driven ports; the inside owns the port protocols
why.forbid: no telemetry, file format, agent SDK or model client in the core, and none of the I/O behind domain/__init__.py's 'Nothing here does I/O': the filesystem, processes, sockets, signals, import machinery, sys. 'open' catches the builtin, which no import check sees

why.domain types: a port is stated in domain types: the agent runtime in agent's, the model runtime in model_call's, the store in construct's and executor's Run, the document source in problems'
why.no matrix.domain.ports: a port never reaches another port: how they combine is the root's
why.forbid: no tracing, no logging and no file format in a port, which would force that opinion on every implementor

why.*: an adapter holds its own technology: yaml, rich, fcntl and sockets, the Claude Agent SDK, hardline (each technology confined to one file by single_importer)
why.matrix.domain: the port it implements and the domain types it speaks in
why.not matrix.adapters or matrix.compositio: an adapter reaches no other adapter and does no wiring: one place chooses adapters
why.forbid opentelemetry: the OpenTelemetry API is spoken by the otel observer alone, and the SDK is installed by the root's telemetry module alone

why.*: the OpenTelemetry API, and importlib.metadata for the instrumentation scope's version
why.matrix.domain.observer: an observer needs only the Event type and the event names; nothing else of matrix

why.signals: turns SIGTERM and SIGINT into cancellation: process technology, reaching no part of matrix
why.skill: renders the --skill text from the domain's declared names (errors, ids, the registry's points, the steps' types)

why.matrix: the command reaches matrix through 'import matrix' alone. The entry admits every matrix.* path, since an allowance is a prefix; tests/test_architecture.py holds the command to matrix.__all__
why.forbid: naming a concrete adapter in the command is a second wiring

why.*: matrix.process is a public helper a component calls (start, kill_group): process technology, reaching no part of matrix

why.*, matrix: the composition root chooses adapters, wires ports and holds configuration; the package __init__ re-exports the public surface
why.forbid opentelemetry: the root installs telemetry through composition/telemetry.py alone

why.*: the OpenTelemetry SDK and its OTLP exporters, and the OTEL_* environment: installing a provider is configuration, so it is the root's, and the library itself stays on the API
why.matrix.domain.errors, matrix.domain.prob: a bad telemetry setting is a ConfigError with its problem

single_importer_why: one file per technology: the Claude Agent SDK behind the agent runtime port, hardline behind the model runtime port, YAML behind the document source (FileSource hides the file formats), rich-click behind the command. OpenTelemetry is two files by design, the API in the otel observer and the SDK in the root's telemetry module, so it is confined by 'forbid' in every other layer rather than by a single_importer rule
